met_analysis:
The cyclonic storm “Arnab” [Pronunciation :Ornab]” over Eastcentral and adjoining Westcentral Bay of Bengal moved nearly westwards with a speed of 13 kmph during last 6 hours and lies centered at 1130 hrs IST of today, the 26th October, 2026 over Westcentral & adjoining Eastcentral Bay of Bengal near latitude 15.5°N and longitude 88.2°E, 550 km southeast of Gopalpur (Odisha), 580 km east-southeast of Vishakhapatnam (Andhra Pradesh), 650 km northwest of Sri Vijaya Puram (Andaman Islands), 660 km east-southeast of Kakinada (Andhra Pradesh), 760 km east-southeast of Machilipatnam (Andhra Pradesh) and 830 km east- southeast of Bapatla (Andhra Pradesh). It is very likely to move west-northwestwards and intensify further into a severe cyclonic storm over westcentral Bay of Bengal by evening of today, the 26th October and into a very severe cyclonic storm over the same region on 27th October. Thereafter, it is very likely to move northwestwards and cross Andhra Pradesh & Yanam coasts between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam close to Yanam as a very severe cyclonic storm with the maximum sustained wind speed of 115-125 kmph gusting to 140 kmph by forenoon of 28th October, 2026.
The Low Pressure areaover Southwest Bay of Bengal and adjoining south coastal Tamil Nadu persisted over the same region at 1430 hrs IST of today, the 26th October, 2026. The associated cyclonic circulation extends upto 7.6 km above mean sea level.
The trough from Lakshadweep Area to the cyclonic circulation associated with the low pressure area over Southwest Bay of Bengal and adjoining south coastal Tamil Nadu across South Kerala extending upto 3.1 km above mean sea level persists.
The Western Disturbance as a cyclonic circulation over north Haryana between 3.1 & 4.5 km above mean sea level persists.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over Southwest Rajasthan & neighbourhood at 1.5 km above mean sea level persists.
The Western Disturbance as a trough in middle & upper tropospheric westerlies with its axis at 5.8 km above mean sea level now runs roughly along Long. 70°E to the north of Lat. 25°N. it is likely to affect northwest India from the night of 27th October, 2026.
